deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck sets up the general factorization problem. M is a category and Φ0 ⊂ Fl(M) is a class of arrows. Ψ is the class of arrows with the right lifting property (RLP) with respect to Φ0. Φ̄0 is the class of arrows with the left lifting property with respect to Ψ, i.e. the saturation of Φ0. Φ is any intermediate class Φ0 ⊂ Φ ⊂ Φ̄0. He wants conditions under which (Φ, Ψ) is a factorization system in the weak sense: every f factors as f = p∘i with i ∈ Φ and p ∈ Ψ.

Step 1 (the one-step construction). Fix f : X → Y. Take all commutative squares D, namely v : A → X, u : B → Y and g : A → B in Φ0 with f∘v = u∘g. Each square gives a pushout X_D = X ⊔_A B and an induced map p_D : X_D → Y. Then form X1(f) as the amalgamated sum of all the X_D under X. This is equivalently the single pushout of ⊔_D g along the map ⊔_D A → X. The result is a factorization X → X1(f) → Y, written i1(f) followed by Σ1(f), and one hopes i1(f) ∈ Φ.

He lists the hypotheses needed:
- (a) Φ0 is small.
- (b) M has amalgamated sums indexed by sets of cardinality ≤ card Φ0. This is refined to card Φ0 × C, with C the supremum of card Hom(A,X) × card Hom(B,Y) over g : A → B in Φ0. That is the correct bound on the number of squares D.
- (c) Φ is stable under cobase change along Φ0-maps and under filtered colimits of bounded size (≤ γ).

Step 2 (transfinite iteration). For successors, Σ_{α+1}(f) = Σ1(Σ_α(f)) and i_{α+1} = i1(Σ_α f) ∘ i_α. For limit ordinals, Σ_α(f) is the colimit of the Σ_{α'}(f) for α' < α. Φ must be stable under these transfinite composites. The length α0 is to be fixed later via a cardinal π. π is chosen so that the source and target of every g ∈ Φ0 are π-accessible: Hom(A,−) commutes with π-filtered colimits. One may take π = sup_g π_g.

The page breaks off here. The intended conclusion is the usual one: at a π-filtered stage α0, any square from g ∈ Φ0 into Σ_{α0}(f) factors through some earlier stage. Hence Σ_{α0}(f) ∈ Ψ, giving the factorization. This is exactly Quillen's small object argument, set in an axiomatic frame with an intermediate class Φ and explicit cardinal bookkeeping.
errors: The notation for lifting classes is muddled. Ψ is written (Φ0^*)_*, while Φ̄0 is written Ψ^*. With consistent conventions Ψ should be just the right-lifting class of Φ0, and Φ̄0 its left-lifting class. There is a marginal correction mark ('B') at this spot, and the top note 'we do not use Φ ⊂ Φ0^*' adds to the confusion.
Requiring the targets of the generating maps to be π-accessible is superfluous. For the standard argument only the sources need to be small. This is harmless.

The exact successor-step requirement is never stated as one condition. It is that Φ be stable under pushouts of coproducts of Φ0-maps and under composition. Composition was written in hypothesis (b) and then crossed out.

Condition (c) is not yet consistent with the limit-step requirement. It bounds filtered colimits by card Φ0 (or γ), but the colimits needed are transfinite composites of length up to α0, which depends on π. He acknowledges this gap with 'do with this γ in mind' and the extra assumption at the end.
The argument is unfinished: the final step, showing Σ_{α0}(f) ∈ Ψ via accessibility, is not written.

ideas.what: One-step factorization by pushing out all Φ0-squares over f at once (amalgamated sum under X of the X ⊔_A B)
ideas.modern_name: Step of the small object argument
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Pursuing Stacks (1983) discussions of model structures; unsure

ideas.what: Transfinite iteration of the one-step factorization, with stopping ordinal determined by accessibility of the generating maps' sources
ideas.modern_name: Small object argument / cofibrantly generated weak factorization systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen 1967; Bousfield 1977; general form in Hovey, Hirschhorn, Beke, Lurie

ideas.what: Working with an arbitrary intermediate class Φ0 ⊂ Φ ⊂ Φ̄0 satisfying closure conditions, rather than only the saturation
ideas.modern_name: Factorization with respect to a class containing the cell complexes (relative cell complexes ⊂ saturation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the cofibrantly generated model category literature (e.g. Hirschhorn, Hovey)

ideas.what: Explicit cardinal bounds on the colimits required: card Φ0 × sup card Hom(A,X) × card Hom(B,Y)
ideas.modern_name: Size bookkeeping in the small object argument (existence of κ-small colimits suffices)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; locally presentable category literature (Gabriel–Ulmer 1971, Adámek–Rosický)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, partially finished private reconstruction of Quillen's small object argument. It is minimally generalized: an intermediate class Φ, size-bounded colimits only, and accessibility via π. All of this is standard by 1982, so nothing here would be new to a specialist. Its only interest is historical, documenting Grothendieck working through the argument (c. 1982–83) in connection with stacks and model structures.
transcription_corrections: The first-line definition of Ψ is likely meant as the right-orthogonal Φ0^* (the class with RLP), with a marginal 'B' correction; the transcribed '(Φ0^*)_*' reflects Grothendieck's own inconsistent notation.
In (c), '{+or than ≤ γ+}' should read roughly 'or rather ≤ γ' (an inserted alternative bound γ, written above), matching the margin note 'do with this γ in mind'.
In (b), the insertion reads approximately '(or rather, when, card Φ0 × C, where C is sup(card Hom(A,X) × card Hom(B,Y)) for u : A → B in Φ0)'.
The successor-step formula Σ_{α+1}(f) = Σ1(Σ_α(f)) is written twice on the page (once in the brace, once beside the diagram); this is not a different statement.
Final line: 'for any g ∈ Φ0, source and target of g are π-accessible' replaces the crossed-out 'all objects of Φ0'; the page breaks off at 'where'.
